newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark consolidates, rally not over.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark consolidates, rally not over.

text.p: Dollar/mark, after a retreat prompted by Bundesbank officials' comments, is set to reconquer higher ground on the way to meeting a medium-term objective at 1.8075/95, analysts said on Tuesday.
The dollar surged above 1.80 marks for the first time since August 1991 and took out 1.8025 resistance before retreating to 1.7930/40 at the close, unchanged from the open.

Prompting the slide were Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler's remarks about the dollar rally being overdone while German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said his administration will endorse a strong mark and a strong euro.

Chartists said dollar/mark remained bullish in a consolidation near 1.7940, an important level from where a breakout higher in a six-week rising channel took place on Monday, paving the way for Tuesday's foray above 1.80.
That bullish breakout allowed to meet an objective at 1.8025, now the near-term resistance. Reconquering that level would set the next target in an area that chartists put at 1.8075 to 1.8095.
"I see 1.80 again, and very soon, on the way to 1.84, and maybe even higher, later," said Merrill Lynch First vice President David Horner.
Dollar/yen rallied on comments by Japan's vice minister for international affairs Eisuke Sakakibara who called market anticipation of a stronger yen too high.
Unlike dollar/mark, dollar/yen retained most of its gains to end at 115.74/79 vs. 114.38/43.
"Closing above 115.50, we have a bull flag," said Sakura Bank assistant vice president Doug Lee. "Now, a close above 116.10 would be a very significant close."
Chartists said 117.00 remained a key level for dollar/yen since it is the 38-percent retracement of the move from the 1997 high of 127.46 to the year's low at 110.62.
Lee remained very bullish on dollar/mark as he remarked that "oral intervention..." such as the German remarks made on Tuesday, "... won't work for long."
Meanwhile, mark/yen rebounded. But chartists cautioned the recovery won't be confirmed unless 65.55, previously a key support and now a major resistance, is regained.

As for dollar/Swiss, it slipped in synchronicity with dollar/mark. To restart that rally would require recapturing 1.48, a big level that was briefly taken out on Tuesday. Down the road would be the retest of 1.4922, the 1997 high.
